scope: Bounded public assessment of UNIFIL–UNSCOL proposed vehicles, ICT and consumables; vehicle child scope covers all six UF01 proposal positions. Public question dispositions are separate from F03 candidate states.

questions.question: Does the proposed asset reuse present a credible efficiency opportunity?
questions.answer: Yes, as a public proposal to satisfy recipient requirements with existing assets. Lower net cost and feasible safe release remain unproved.
questions.interpretation: The bounded vehicle review covers all six proposal positions: four light and two armoured vehicles. These are not six authenticated physical assets. UF02 ICT and UF03 consumables are outside that child cohort.
alternative_explanations: New acquisition or retention may be preferable if condition, remaining life, donor demand or transport/support cost makes reuse unsuitable.
limits: Actual recipient need, available inventory, asset condition, equivalent alternative and canceled commitments are unavailable.
The retained budget transcription is not freshly authenticated final budget text.
questions.next_action: Retain the public opportunity as conditional; use the existing E02/addendum if evidence becomes available.
questions.reopen_trigger: An adopted applicable budget or a complete mapped six-position cohort with documented need, alternatives, protected donor capability and full costs becomes public or is lawfully supplied.

questions.question: Does public authority authorize the specific UNIFIL-to-UNSCOL transfer?
questions.answer: No specific recipient or lot approval is established by the reviewed public evidence. Resolution2790 OP9 supplies general designated-entity transfer language, subject to UN practices and financial rules.
questions.interpretation: Final Council text and founding letters establish the legal context; UNSCOL political coordination does not confer lot-specific property or procurement approval.
alternative_explanations: Competent designation, delegated approval or transfer documentation may exist outside the reviewed public record.
limits: No exhaustive later amendment, administrative delegation or recipient-designation review.
Absence of public approval evidence is not proof that a transfer would be unlawful.
questions.next_action: Record the approval question as unresolved and make no actual-transfer assertion.
questions.reopen_trigger: A competent designation, donor release and recipient acceptance covering the actual assets, or a definitive public instrument, is obtained.

questions.question: Can the embedded amounts be counted as a new project benefit?
questions.answer: No. The retained proposal already includes USD394000 for vehicles and USD438100 across vehicles, ICT and consumables. Adding the vehicle amount again to that aggregate would duplicate the same proposal component.
questions.interpretation: This is a supported accounting concern about potential double counting, not evidence that the UN has duplicated spending or that the project has already booked a duplicate benefit.
alternative_explanations: The total and vehicle component may legitimately appear separately as an aggregate and its breakdown if clearly labeled nonadditive.
limits: Primary Add.4 budget text was not freshly authenticated; no GA adoption or actual expenditure established.
There is no recognized project benefit and no quantified incremental opportunity.
questions.next_action: Keep the components and aggregate linked, with the aggregate nonadditive to its components.
questions.reopen_trigger: Authenticated source corrections or a separately evidenced incremental counterfactual changes the classification; financial recognition requires its own gate.

questions.question: Should donor assets be released on the strength of the proposal alone?
questions.answer: No. Retain applicable approved custody, procurement and release procedures until competent authorities establish safe availability and recipient suitability; this assessment recommends no transfer execution.
questions.interpretation: OP6 protects withdrawal functions including security, enabling and medical capability. OP7 liquidation and residual guards and OP9 financial-rule requirements remain material constraints; a calendar-2027 recipient proposal does not accelerate donor release.
alternative_explanations: Some assets may be genuinely surplus before others, and a documented asset-specific release could be appropriate.
limits: No asset-level donor readiness reservation or approved release timetable is established.
Retaining current procedures is a public decision disposition, not an F03 terminal state for the parent or child.
questions.next_action: Preserve current controls and all six proposal-position outcomes, including retained, unavailable, rejected or substituted assets.
questions.reopen_trigger: Documented current donor need, condition, protected-function clearance, recipient need and competent release/acceptance permit a fresh decision.

questions.question: Can public evidence establish waste, completed transfers or net financial results?
questions.answer: No. Public sources support a proposal and transition constraints, but do not authenticate completed handovers, canceled procurement, service performance or a net whole-life cost result.
questions.interpretation: The historical joint vehicle-washing EOI is evidence of a shared procurement intention at its date, not an award, current contract, asset transfer or proof of waste. Unknown results stay unknown.
alternative_explanations: Transfers may be beneficial, neutral, costly or not implemented; necessary donor retention or noncancelable acquisition can explain lack of a benefit.
limits: No current signed transfers, linked inventories, commitments or matched full costs.
Book value, proposal reduction and cash effects have different meanings; calendar-2027 SPM and July–June peacekeeping periods are not directly subtractable.
questions.next_action: Close this bounded public review with explicit limitations rather than postpone its conclusion indefinitely for inaccessible records. Preserve the reopen route and no benefit recognition.
questions.reopen_trigger: A reliable public audit, transfer/performance report or authorized linked record set establishes implementation, equivalent need, total external costs and service outcomes.

Arithmetic aggregate of the three components; do not add to them or add394000 again. Already embedded in retained proposal transcription; primary budget not freshly authenticated. Not adopted funding, actual expenditure or a validated benefit.

proposed_responsible_roles.purpose: Maintain the public assessment, track official source updates and reopen individual questions when documented triggers are met; no institutional approval or operational direction.

proposed_responsible_roles.role: UNIFIL donor property/transition and UNSCOL recipient property/procurement/finance custodians
proposed_responsible_roles.purpose: If separately authorized and willing, clarify designation, protected donor need, all-six-position mapping, recipient requirement and full costs through existing E02 channels.

case_synthesis.overall_judgment: Public evidence supports a conditional reuse opportunity and a specific accounting caution against double counting embedded proposal estimates. It does not establish waste, specific transfer approval, implementation or net financial benefit; donor safeguards justify retaining applicable current release controls.
case_synthesis.recommended_decision: Complete the bounded public review with limitations; retain the opportunity as conditional and current release controls, recognize no benefit, and reopen only the affected questions when their documented evidence triggers are met. Assign source monitoring to a proposed project research maintainer; do not imply institutional acceptance or dispatch requests.
